The completion rates count pending orders as not completed. Partner has about 20% pending against about 14% for direct, and those shares are flat across January, February and March, so the gap is not an end-of-quarter censoring effect. Both test p-values are stored as 0.0000000000 with display_digits 4. Rendered literally they read as a p of exactly zero, but they are only below the display precision, so the release should show them as below 0.0001.

Both registered tests declare bonferroni with alpha 0.05, but the register does not write down the per-test threshold of 0.025. Both p-values are far below it, so the conclusions stand, but the correction is stated rather than shown.

The hypothesis blocks in analysis/answers/R03.json and R04.json name the method, alpha, correction and n per group but not the groups or their order. summary: Every number in the eight claims matches my independent recount from quarantine/orders.csv (deduplicated by last revision, cut to 2026-01..2026-03 by order_month, negative refunds excluded; 44531 orders), and the claim-to-metric-to-plan chain has no gaps. No confounding by country or month and no Simpson reversal was found. The analysis still fails on wording: CLM-COMPLETION-DIRECT declares its population as delivered orders of the direct channel, but the rate is computed over the whole channel (24597 orders, including 3322 cancelled and 3457 pending).
